# Introduction

This document implements a complete preprocessing pipeline for single-cell RNA-seq data.
The pipeline can create Seurat objects from raw count matrices or AnnData .h5ad files;
the current analysis starts from compressed, tab-delimited raw UMI count matrices and
their corresponding cell annotation files. The workflow performs basic quality control
filtering based on mitochondrial gene expression and prepares the datasets for downstream
analyses such as normalization, clustering, and visualization.


# Libraries

```{r}
library(Matrix)
library(Seurat)
library(reticulate)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(DescTools)
library(scales)
library(ggplot2)
# library(ggvenn)
# library(pals)
library(ggpubr)
library(ggrepel)
library(Nebulosa)
library(scMRMA)

project_dir <- "/home/drighelli/lncRNA_project"

data_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "DATA")

# Reserved for possible AnnData (.h5ad) inputs.
datah_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "DATAH")

# Store all CRC-specific results separately from other outputs.
out_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "OUT", "CRC")

dir.create(
  out_dir,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

source(file.path(project_dir, "functions.R"))
```

# Dataset definition

All datasets to be processed are defined in a single list.
Each entry contains three fields: `counts` is the path to a compressed, tab-delimited raw
UMI count matrix; `meta` is the path to the corresponding cell annotation file; and `save`
is the path where the resulting Seurat object is saved.

To add a new dataset, simply append a new GSE entry to this list.

```{r}
datasets <- list(
  
  GSE144735 = list(
    counts = file.path(data_dir, "GSE144735_processed_KUL3_CRC_10X_raw_UMI_count_matrix.txt.gz"),
    meta = file.path(data_dir, "GSE144735_processed_KUL3_CRC_10X_annotation.txt.gz"),
    save = file.path(out_dir, "obj_GSE144735_qc.rds")
  ),
  
  GSE132465 = list(
    counts = file.path(data_dir, "GSE132465_GEO_processed_CRC_10X_raw_UMI_count_matrix.txt.gz"),
    meta = file.path(data_dir, "GSE132465_GEO_processed_CRC_10X_cell_annotation.txt.gz"),
    save = file.path(out_dir, "obj_GSE132465_qc.rds")
  ),
  
  GSE132257 = list(
    counts = file.path(
      data_dir,
      "GSE132257_GEO_processed_protocol_and_fresh_frozen_raw_UMI_count_matrix.txt.gz"
    ),
    meta = file.path(
      data_dir,
      "GSE132257_processed_protocol_and_fresh_frozen_cell_annotation.txt.gz"
    ),
    save = file.path(out_dir, "obj_GSE132257_qc.rds")
  )
  
)

# To add a fourth dataset:
# simply add another element in the list above following the same structure.
```

# Preprocessing pipeline (loop over datasets)

This loop uses `load_txt_counts_to_seurat()` to process all datasets currently defined
above from raw UMI count matrices and cell annotation files, and stores the resulting
Seurat objects in a list.

```{r}
obj_list <- list()

for (name in names(datasets)) {
  
  cat("Processing dataset:", name, "\n")
  
  obj_list[[name]] <- load_txt_counts_to_seurat(
    counts_file = datasets[[name]]$counts,
    meta_file = datasets[[name]]$meta,
    save_path = datasets[[name]]$save
  )
  
  cat("Completed dataset:", name, "\n\n")
}

print(names(obj_list))

saveRDS(obj_list, file.path(out_dir, "obj_list_all.rds"))

obj_list[[1]]

```

# Merge Datasets

```{r}
merged_obj <- merge_seurat_objects(
  obj_list = obj_list,
  save_path = file.path(out_dir, "merged_seurat_qc.rds")
)

# Check Merged objs

dim(merged_obj)

print(merged_obj)

table(merged_obj$GSE)

head(merged_obj@meta.data)

# Remove obj_list

rm(obj_list)
gc()
```

# QC Visualization

This section evaluates basic quality control metrics across datasets,
including number of detected genes, total counts, and mitochondrial percentage.

```{r}
merged_obj <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "merged_seurat_qc.rds"))
obj <- merged_obj

# define dataset colors (consistent palette)
cols <- scales::hue_pal()(length(unique(obj$GSE)))

VlnPlot(
  obj,
  features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA", "percent.mt"),
  group.by = "GSE",
  cols = cols,
  ncol = 3,
  pt.size = 0
)
```

# Dimensionality Reduction

This section performs normalization, feature selection, scaling,
PCA, and UMAP embedding for downstream visualization.

```{r}
obj <- NormalizeData(obj)

obj <- FindVariableFeatures(
  obj,
  selection.method = "vst",
  nfeatures = 2000
)

obj <- ScaleData(obj, features = VariableFeatures(obj))

obj <- RunPCA(obj, features = VariableFeatures(obj), npcs = 30)

ElbowPlot(obj)

obj <- RunUMAP(obj, dims = 1:15)
```


# Save Processed Object

Save the processed Seurat object after normalization and dimensionality reduction.

```{r}
saveRDS(
  obj,
  file.path(out_dir, "merged_normalized_hvgs.rds")
)
```


# UMAP Visualization

This section visualizes batch effects across datasets using UMAP.

```{r}
DimPlot(obj, group.by = "GSE", cols = cols) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

# Cell type specificity

This section quantifies cell type specificity of lncRNAs and protein-coding genes
using the Gini coefficient computed from DotPlot-based expression summaries.

```{r}
obj <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "merged_seurat_qc.rds"))

obj <- seurat_preprocess(obj)

gencode <- read.table(file.path(data_dir, "gencode_v49_compatible.txt"), header = TRUE)

gene_sets <- gene_biotype_matching(obj, gencode)

lnc_features <- gene_sets$lnc
prot_features <- gene_sets$prot
ambiguous_genes <- gene_sets$ambiguous

chunk_size <- 2000

GiniCoef_lnc <- compute_gini_pipeline(obj, lnc_features, "lncRNA", chunk_size)
GiniCoef_prot <- compute_gini_pipeline(obj, prot_features, "protein_coding", chunk_size)

GiniCoef <- rbind(GiniCoef_lnc, GiniCoef_prot)
colnames(GiniCoef)[1] <- "gene"

saveRDS(GiniCoef, file.path(out_dir, "gini_dotplot_v49.rds"))

GiniCoef <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "gini_dotplot_v49.rds"))

GiniCoef_clean <- GiniCoef[!is.na(GiniCoef$gini), ]

lnc_n  <- nrow(GiniCoef_clean %>% filter(type == "lncRNA"))
prot_n <- nrow(GiniCoef_clean %>% filter(type == "protein_coding"))

plot_gini_results(GiniCoef_clean, lnc_n, prot_n)
```

# GRN Expression Filtering

## STEP 1: Calculate Expression Statistics

Objective:
- summarize gene expression across pseudobulk samples
- inspect the expression distribution
- support an informed choice of filtering thresholds

No genes are removed at this stage.

```{r}
grn_expression_qc <- calculate_grn_expression_statistics(
  expression_matrix = grn_pseudobulk_logcpm,
  count_matrix = grn_pseudobulk_counts
)

summary(grn_expression_qc$mean_logcpm)

summary(grn_expression_qc$median_logcpm)

summary(grn_expression_qc$n_detected_pseudobulk)
```

## STEP 2: Inspect Expression Distribution

Objective:

- visualize gene expression across pseudobulk samples
- identify genes with very low detection
- support the selection of filtering thresholds

No filtering is applied at this stage.

```{r}
grn_expression_plots <- plot_grn_expression_distribution(
  expression_statistics = grn_expression_qc
)

grn_expression_plots$mean_logcpm

grn_expression_plots$detected_pseudobulk
```

## STEP 3: Select Filtering Thresholds

Objective:

- define expression-based filtering criteria for GRN construction

The initial GRN analysis is performed without expression filtering.

Filtering thresholds will be defined after validating the unfiltered GRN
workflow and evaluating the impact of expression filtering on lncRNA
representation.

## STEP 4: Apply Expression Filtering

Objective:

- remove lowly expressed genes according to the selected thresholds

Expression filtering will be applied after validating the unfiltered GRN
workflow, allowing a direct comparison between filtered and unfiltered
networks.

# Spearman Correlation Analysis

## STEP 1: Prepare Unfiltered GRN Expression Matrix

Objective:

- restrict the normalized pseudobulk matrix to lncRNA and protein-coding genes
- preserve all GRN candidate genes before correlation analysis
- identify genes with zero variance across pseudobulk samples

No genes are removed at this stage.

```{r}
grn_correlation_input <- prepare_grn_correlation_matrix(
  expression_matrix = grn_pseudobulk_logcpm,
  gene_sets = grn_gene_sets
)

dim(grn_correlation_input$expression)

length(grn_correlation_input$zero_variance_genes)

grn_correlation_input$n_genes

grn_correlation_input$n_samples
```

## STEP 2: Compute Unfiltered Spearman Correlations

Objective:

- compute pairwise Spearman correlations across all GRN candidate genes
- preserve the complete gene-gene correlation matrix
- establish the unfiltered baseline for downstream GRN construction

No correlation threshold is applied at this stage.

```{r}
grn_spearman_matrix <- compute_grn_spearman_correlations(
  expression_matrix = grn_correlation_input$expression
)

dim(grn_spearman_matrix)

sum(is.na(grn_spearman_matrix))

range(grn_spearman_matrix)

saveRDS(grn_spearman_matrix, file.path(grn_out_dir, "grn_spearman_unfiltered.rds"))
```

# Correlation Network Filtering

## STEP 1: Inspect Correlation Strength Distribution

Objective:

- summarize pairwise Spearman correlations across GRN candidate genes
- quantify the number of gene pairs retained at different correlation strengths
- support an informed choice of correlation thresholds

No correlation filtering is applied at this stage.

```{r}
# grn_spearman_matrix <- readRDS(file.path(grn_out_dir, "grn_spearman_unfiltered.rds"))
grn_correlation_summary <- summarize_grn_correlations(
  correlation_matrix = grn_spearman_matrix
)

grn_correlation_summary$summary

grn_correlation_summary$threshold_counts

grn_spearman_distribution_plot <- plot_grn_spearman_distribution(
  correlation_matrix = grn_spearman_matrix
)

grn_spearman_distribution_plot
```

## STEP 2: Inspect Correlations by Gene-Pair Type

Objective:

- characterize correlations according to gene-pair type
- distinguish lncRNA-lncRNA, lncRNA-protein-coding, and protein-coding pairs
- evaluate lncRNA representation across different correlation strengths

No correlation filtering is applied at this stage.

```{r}
grn_correlation_by_type <- summarize_grn_correlations_by_gene_type(
  correlation_matrix = grn_spearman_matrix,
  gene_sets = grn_gene_sets
)

grn_correlation_by_type
```

## STEP 3: Inspect Correlation Structure by Gene Detection

Objective:

- evaluate whether strong correlations are associated with low gene detection
- compare detection patterns across lncRNA and protein-coding genes
- assess whether highly correlated gene pairs are supported across pseudobulk samples

No genes or correlations are removed at this stage.

```{r}
grn_correlation_detection_summary <-
  summarize_grn_correlations_by_detection(
    correlation_matrix = grn_spearman_matrix,
    expression_statistics = grn_expression_qc,
    gene_sets = grn_gene_sets
  )

grn_correlation_detection_summary
```

# GRN Expression Filtering - Finalization

The unfiltered GRN validation showed that the complete workflow preserves
lncRNA representation, but strong correlations are largely associated with
genes detected in very few pseudobulk samples.

The expression filtering workflow introduced previously is therefore completed
at this stage before final network inference.

## STEP 3: Select Filtering Thresholds

Objective:

- define expression-based filtering criteria based on the observed detection
  patterns
- reduce correlations driven by poorly detected genes
- preserve lncRNA representation for downstream GRN inference

```{r}
grn_detection_thresholds <- evaluate_grn_detection_thresholds(
  expression_statistics = grn_expression_qc,
  gene_sets = grn_gene_sets
)

grn_detection_thresholds

grn_detection_threshold_plots <- plot_grn_detection_thresholds(
  detection_thresholds = grn_detection_thresholds,
  selected_threshold = 2
)

grn_detection_threshold_plots$retained_counts

grn_detection_threshold_plots$retention_proportion
```

A minimum detection threshold of 2 pseudobulk samples was selected for the
CRC dataset.

This conservative threshold removes genes that are never detected or detected
in only one pseudobulk sample, which were found to strongly contribute to the
high correlations observed in the unfiltered CRC analysis.

The selected threshold retains 3,223 lncRNA genes, preserving substantial
lncRNA representation for downstream CRC GRN inference.

## STEP 4: Apply Expression Filtering

Objective:

- remove genes that do not satisfy the selected expression criteria
- generate the filtered expression matrix used for final GRN inference
- retain the unfiltered analysis as a baseline for comparison

```{r}
grn_filtered <- apply_grn_expression_filter(
  expression_matrix = grn_pseudobulk_logcpm,
  count_matrix = grn_pseudobulk_counts,
  expression_statistics = grn_expression_qc,
  gene_sets = grn_gene_sets,
  min_detected_pseudobulk = 2
)

dim(grn_filtered$expression)

length(grn_filtered$gene_sets$lnc)

length(grn_filtered$gene_sets$prot)

length(grn_filtered$retained_genes)

length(grn_filtered$removed_genes)

saveRDS(grn_filtered, file.path(grn_out_dir, "grn_filtered.rds"))
```

# GENIE3 Network Inference

## STEP 1: Prepare Candidate Regulators

Objective:

- identify human transcription factors supported by the curated Human TF database
- restrict candidate regulators to protein-coding genes retained after CRC expression filtering
- prepare a biologically informed regulator set for GENIE3 inference

```{r}
human_tf <- read.delim(file.path(data_dir, "DatabaseExtract_v_1.01.txt"), header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

grn_genie3_regulators <- prepare_genie3_regulators(
  human_tf = human_tf,
  filtered_gene_sets = grn_filtered$gene_sets,
  expression_matrix = grn_filtered$expression
)

length(grn_genie3_regulators)

head(grn_genie3_regulators)
```

## STEP 2: Configure GENIE3 Inference

Objective:

- define reproducible GENIE3 inference parameters
- use curated transcription factors as candidate regulators
- retain all filtered GRN genes as potential targets

```{r}
grn_genie3_config <- list(
  tree_method = "RF",
  K = "sqrt",
  n_trees = 1000,
  n_cores = 8
)

grn_genie3_config
```

## STEP 3: Run GENIE3 Network Inference

Objective:

- infer directed regulatory relationships from filtered pseudobulk expression
- use curated transcription factors as candidate regulators
- retain all filtered genes as potential targets
- compute GENIE3 importance scores using Random Forests

```{r}
set.seed(grn_config$random_seed)

grn_genie3_weights <- GENIE3::GENIE3(
  exprMatrix = as.matrix(grn_filtered$expression),
  regulators = grn_genie3_regulators,
  treeMethod = grn_genie3_config$tree_method,
  K = grn_genie3_config$K,
  nTrees = grn_genie3_config$n_trees,
  nCores = grn_genie3_config$n_cores
)

saveRDS(grn_genie3_weights, file.path(grn_out_dir, "grn_genie3_weights.rds"))

dim(grn_genie3_weights)
sum(is.na(grn_genie3_weights))
range(grn_genie3_weights)
```

# Spearman and GENIE3 Integration

## STEP 1: Integrate GENIE3 and Spearman Results

Objective:

- combine GENIE3 importance scores with Spearman correlations
- associate each candidate TF-target interaction with its expression correlation
- retain the direction of regulation inferred by GENIE3 and the sign of the corresponding Spearman correlation
- prepare candidate regulatory interactions for GRN construction

```{r}
# grn_genie3_weights <- readRDS(file.path(grn_out_dir, "grn_genie3_weights.rds"))
grn_integrated_edges <- integrate_genie3_spearman(
  genie3_weights = grn_genie3_weights,
  spearman_matrix = grn_spearman_matrix
)

dim(grn_integrated_edges)

head(grn_integrated_edges)

summary(grn_integrated_edges$genie3_weight)

summary(grn_integrated_edges$spearman_rho)

sum(is.na(grn_integrated_edges))
```

## STEP 2: Inspect Integrated Edge Score Distributions

Objective:

- characterize the distribution of GENIE3 importance scores
- evaluate the strength of Spearman correlations among candidate interactions
- assess the effect of different score thresholds on network size
- support an informed selection of criteria for GRN construction

No interactions are removed at this stage.

```{r}
grn_integrated_summary <- summarize_grn_integrated_edges(
  integrated_edges = grn_integrated_edges
)

grn_integrated_summary$genie3_summary

grn_integrated_summary$spearman_summary

grn_integrated_summary$genie3_quantiles

grn_integrated_summary$threshold_counts

grn_genie3_importance_plot <- plot_grn_genie3_importance_distribution(
  integrated_edges = grn_integrated_edges
)

grn_genie3_importance_plot

grn_threshold_selection_plot <- plot_grn_threshold_selection(
  threshold_counts = grn_integrated_summary$threshold_counts,
  selected_genie3_quantile = 0.995,
  selected_spearman_threshold = 0.5
)

grn_threshold_selection_plot
```

## STEP 3: Evaluate Candidate Network Composition

Objective:

- evaluate network composition across candidate GENIE3 and Spearman thresholds
- quantify lncRNA representation in candidate networks
- compare network size with preservation of biologically relevant targets
- support the final selection of GRN construction criteria

No final network threshold is selected at this stage.

```{r}
grn_candidate_networks <- evaluate_grn_candidate_networks(
  integrated_edges = grn_integrated_edges,
  filtered_gene_sets = grn_filtered$gene_sets,
  genie3_quantile_table = grn_integrated_summary$genie3_quantiles
)

grn_candidate_networks

grn_lnc_retention_plot <- plot_grn_lnc_retention_vs_network_size(
  candidate_networks = grn_candidate_networks,
  selected_genie3_quantile = 0.995,
  selected_spearman_threshold = 0.5
)

grn_lnc_retention_plot
```

## STEP 4: Evaluate lncRNA Edge Representation

Objective:

- quantify regulatory interactions targeting lncRNA and protein-coding genes
- compare lncRNA edge representation across selected candidate networks
- verify that candidate thresholds preserve substantial lncRNA connectivity
- support the final selection of GRN construction criteria

No final network is constructed at this stage.

```{r}
grn_candidate_settings <- data.frame(
  genie3_quantile = c(0.99, 0.995),
  genie3_cutoff = c(0.008532776, 0.011259691),
  spearman_threshold = c(0.5, 0.5)
)

grn_lnc_edge_representation <- evaluate_grn_lnc_edge_representation(
  integrated_edges = grn_integrated_edges,
  filtered_gene_sets = grn_filtered$gene_sets,
  candidate_settings = grn_candidate_settings
)

grn_lnc_edge_representation
```

# GRN Construction

## STEP 1: Construct Final GRN

Objective:

- apply the selected GENIE3 and Spearman criteria
- retain high-confidence TF-target regulatory interactions
- preserve GENIE3 importance and Spearman correlation as edge attributes
- generate the final CRC GRN edge list for downstream network analysis

```{r}
grn_final_edges <- construct_final_grn(
  integrated_edges = grn_integrated_edges,
  genie3_cutoff = 0.011259691,
  spearman_threshold = 0.5
)

dim(grn_final_edges)

head(grn_final_edges)

table(grn_final_edges$correlation_sign)

length(unique(grn_final_edges$regulator))

length(unique(grn_final_edges$target))

saveRDS(grn_final_edges, file.path(grn_out_dir, "grn_final_edges.rds"))
```

## STEP 2: Prepare GRN Node Table

Objective:

- identify all genes represented in the final GRN
- classify nodes according to gene biotype
- identify transcription factor regulators
- prepare node annotations for downstream network analysis

```{r}
grn_nodes <- prepare_grn_node_table(
  grn_edges = grn_final_edges,
  gene_sets = grn_filtered$gene_sets,
  tf_regulators = grn_genie3_regulators
)

dim(grn_nodes)

head(grn_nodes)

table(grn_nodes$gene_type)

table(grn_nodes$is_tf)

table(grn_nodes$is_regulator, grn_nodes$is_target)

saveRDS(grn_nodes, file.path(grn_out_dir, "grn_nodes.rds"))
```

# GRN Hub Analysis

## STEP 1: Calculate Node Connectivity

Objective:

- calculate in-degree, out-degree, and total degree for each GRN node
- identify highly connected regulatory and target genes
- prepare node-level network metrics for hub analysis

```{r}
grn_node_connectivity <- calculate_grn_node_connectivity(
  grn_edges = grn_final_edges,
  grn_nodes = grn_nodes
)

dim(grn_node_connectivity)

summary(grn_node_connectivity$out_degree)

summary(grn_node_connectivity$in_degree)

summary(grn_node_connectivity$total_degree)

head(
  grn_node_connectivity[
    order(-grn_node_connectivity$total_degree),
  ]
)

saveRDS(grn_node_connectivity, file.path(grn_out_dir, "grn_node_connectivity.rds"))
```

## STEP 2: Evaluate Hub Connectivity Thresholds

Objective:

- evaluate high-connectivity thresholds for regulatory, target, and global hubs
- characterize the upper tail of node degree distributions
- quantify the number of nodes retained at different connectivity quantiles
- support a data-driven definition of GRN hubs

```{r}
grn_hub_thresholds <- evaluate_grn_hub_thresholds(
  node_connectivity = grn_node_connectivity
)

grn_hub_thresholds
```

## STEP 3: Identify GRN Hubs

Objective:

- identify regulatory hubs based on high out-degree
- identify target hubs based on high in-degree
- identify global hubs based on high total degree
- retain node annotations and connectivity metrics for downstream analysis

```{r}
grn_hubs <- identify_grn_hubs(
  node_connectivity = grn_node_connectivity,
  hub_quantile = 0.99
)

grn_hubs$thresholds

nrow(grn_hubs$regulatory_hubs)

nrow(grn_hubs$target_hubs)

nrow(grn_hubs$global_hubs)

head(grn_hubs$regulatory_hubs)

grn_regulatory_hub_plot <- plot_grn_regulatory_hubs(
  regulatory_hubs = grn_hubs$regulatory_hubs
)

grn_regulatory_hub_plot

head(grn_hubs$target_hubs)

head(grn_hubs$global_hubs)

saveRDS(grn_hubs, file.path(grn_out_dir, "grn_hubs.rds"))
```

## STEP 4: Analyze lncRNA Regulatory Connectivity

Objective:

- quantify lncRNA targets associated with each regulatory hub
- distinguish lncRNA and protein-coding connectivity among regulatory hubs
- identify transcription factors with strong connectivity to lncRNA targets
- characterize the contribution of lncRNA interactions to hub regulatory profiles

```{r}
grn_hub_lnc_connectivity <- analyze_grn_hub_lnc_connectivity(
  grn_edges = grn_final_edges,
  regulatory_hubs = grn_hubs$regulatory_hubs,
  gene_sets = grn_filtered$gene_sets
)

grn_hub_lnc_connectivity

grn_hub_lnc_connectivity_plot <- plot_grn_hub_lnc_connectivity(
  hub_lnc_connectivity = grn_hub_lnc_connectivity
)

grn_hub_lnc_connectivity_plot

saveRDS(grn_hub_lnc_connectivity, file.path(grn_out_dir, "grn_hub_lnc_connectivity.rds"))
```

## STEP 5: Analyze lncRNA Target Hubs

Objective:

- identify lncRNA genes among high in-degree target hubs
- quantify their regulatory connectivity
- characterize the number and strength of TF interactions targeting lncRNA hubs
- prepare lncRNA target hubs for downstream visualization and biological interpretation

```{r}
grn_lnc_target_hubs <- analyze_grn_lnc_target_hubs(
  grn_edges = grn_final_edges,
  target_hubs = grn_hubs$target_hubs,
  gene_sets = grn_filtered$gene_sets
)

dim(grn_lnc_target_hubs)

head(grn_lnc_target_hubs, 10)

saveRDS(grn_lnc_target_hubs, file.path(grn_out_dir, "grn_lnc_target_hubs.rds"))
```

# GRN Visualization

## STEP 1: Prepare Regulatory Hub-lncRNA Subnetwork

Objective:

- extract regulatory interactions between GRN regulatory hubs and lncRNA targets
- preserve GENIE3 importance and Spearman correlation as edge attributes
- prepare a focused and interpretable subnetwork for GRN visualization

```{r}
grn_hub_lnc_subnetwork <- prepare_grn_hub_lnc_subnetwork(
  grn_edges = grn_final_edges,
  regulatory_hubs = grn_hubs$regulatory_hubs,
  gene_sets = grn_filtered$gene_sets
)

dim(grn_hub_lnc_subnetwork$edges)

dim(grn_hub_lnc_subnetwork$nodes)

table(grn_hub_lnc_subnetwork$nodes$node_type)

head(grn_hub_lnc_subnetwork$edges)

saveRDS(grn_hub_lnc_subnetwork, file.path(grn_out_dir, "grn_hub_lnc_subnetwork.rds"))
```

## STEP 2: Prepare Focused Hub-lncRNA Network

Objective:

- identify lncRNA targets shared by multiple regulatory hubs
- reduce visual complexity while preserving highly connected lncRNA targets
- prepare an interpretable regulatory subnetwork for network visualization

This step is used for visualization only and does not modify the final GRN.

```{r}
grn_focused_hub_lnc_network <- prepare_focused_grn_hub_lnc_network(
  hub_lnc_subnetwork = grn_hub_lnc_subnetwork,
  min_hub_connections = 2
)

dim(grn_focused_hub_lnc_network$edges)

dim(grn_focused_hub_lnc_network$nodes)

table(grn_focused_hub_lnc_network$nodes$node_type)

summary(grn_focused_hub_lnc_network$nodes$degree_in_subnetwork)

saveRDS(grn_focused_hub_lnc_network, file.path(grn_out_dir, "grn_focused_hub_lnc_network.rds"))
```

## STEP 3: Visualize Focused Hub-lncRNA Network

Objective:

- visualize regulatory interactions between major TF hubs and shared lncRNA targets
- distinguish regulatory hubs from lncRNA nodes
- emphasize highly connected nodes while preserving the complete focused subnetwork
- generate an interpretable representation of hub-lncRNA regulatory relationships

Node labeling is simplified for visualization only and does not modify the network.

```{r}
grn_focused_hub_lnc_graph <- plot_focused_grn_hub_lnc_network(
  focused_network = grn_focused_hub_lnc_network,
  top_lnc_labels = 10,
  seed = grn_config$random_seed
)

igraph::vcount(grn_focused_hub_lnc_graph)

igraph::ecount(grn_focused_hub_lnc_graph)
```

## STEP 4: Prepare lncRNA Target Hub Network

Objective:

- visualize highly connected lncRNA target hubs and their incoming TF interactions
- highlight convergence of multiple regulators on selected lncRNA targets
- provide a complementary target-centered view of the GRN

The number of lncRNA hubs displayed is restricted for visualization only and
does not modify the final GRN or hub classification.

```{r}
grn_lnc_target_hub_network <- prepare_grn_lnc_target_hub_network(
  grn_edges = grn_final_edges,
  lnc_target_hubs = grn_lnc_target_hubs,
  top_n = 10
)

dim(grn_lnc_target_hub_network$edges)

dim(grn_lnc_target_hub_network$nodes)

table(grn_lnc_target_hub_network$nodes$node_type)

head(grn_lnc_target_hub_network$edges)

saveRDS(grn_lnc_target_hub_network, file.path(grn_out_dir, "grn_lnc_target_hub_network.rds"))
```

## STEP 5: Visualize lncRNA Target Hub Network

Objective:

- visualize highly connected lncRNA target hubs and their incoming TF interactions
- distinguish lncRNA target hubs from TF regulators
- highlight regulatory convergence on major lncRNA targets
- preserve all interactions contained in the prepared target-centered subnetwork

Node labeling is simplified for visualization only and does not modify the network.

```{r}
grn_lnc_target_hub_graph <- plot_grn_lnc_target_hub_network(
  target_hub_network = grn_lnc_target_hub_network,
  seed = grn_config$random_seed
)
```

# GRN Results Export

## STEP 1: Export Core GRN Results

Objective:

- export the principal GRN edge, node, hub, and lncRNA connectivity tables
- generate human-readable tabular outputs for downstream inspection and reporting
- preserve the RDS objects as reproducible analysis checkpoints

```{r}
grn_exported_files <- export_grn_core_results(
  grn_edges = grn_final_edges,
  grn_nodes = grn_nodes,

)

grn_exported_files
```

## STEP 2: Summarize Final GRN

Objective:

- summarize the principal structural properties of the final CRC GRN
- report node, edge, regulator, target, and gene-biotype composition
- summarize regulatory hub and lncRNA target hub representation
- generate a compact table for reporting and downstream interpretation

```{r}
grn_final_summary <- summarize_final_grn(
  grn_edges = grn_final_edges,
  grn_nodes = grn_nodes,
  hubs = grn_hubs,
  lnc_target_hubs = grn_lnc_target_hubs
)

grn_final_summary

grn_final_composition_plot <- plot_final_grn_gene_composition(
  final_summary = grn_final_summary
)

grn_final_composition_plot

saveRDS(grn_final_summary, file.path(grn_out_dir, "grn_final_summary.rds"))

write.table(
  grn_final_summary,
  file = file.path(grn_out_dir, "tables", "grn_final_summary.tsv"),
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
